Before mode scoring, identify zero-residual alpha across ALL fourteen actual mode histograms from their known nonnegative count sums and actual tile sample count. Evaluate that plane once through the SAME cost helper. Evaluate remaining RGB planes per mode and add exact prepared alpha cost. Keep the ordinary four-plane fallback.
proof: Histogram bank0 is alpha; mode layouts are14*1024 with4*256 counts. Every mode's plane sum equals the actual clipped tile area, including aggregated parent visits.

If every mode's alpha bin0 equals that sample count, nonnegative counts force every other alpha bin to zero. Therefore all fourteen alpha histograms are identical, irrespective of neighboring transparency or source flags.
History, products and baselines are fixed throughout the fourteen mode comparisons. SmallResidualBias and PreparedPredictionEntropy for that alpha plane are therefore identical.

Use the same integer helper for the prepared plane, preserving exact arithmetic/rounding. Integer cost addition may be regrouped only within format-derived Int64 bounds. Preserve exact numeric scores, mode order, ties, neighbor biases and later hierarchy costs.
Do not infer tile opacity from only the first mode, global source flags or a fixture name. The other modes may read translucent neighbors; require actual all-mode histogram eligibility.
